critic_summary: Targeted failure mode: after 5 prior loops the method's hard 'parent-CSVs only' restriction in step 3 had exhausted the cheap CSV-derivable axes (direction L1, time-of-day L2, regime persistence L3, trendiness L4, spread L5). Loop 6's three Tier-A candidates (side, range-position, round-number) were all FALSIFIED and the method's step-5 'weakest-violation' branch then admitted C3 (round-number) despite the data showing the effect lived entirely in low-sample dates. The researcher's own trace named this explicitly ('the on-disk-CSV restriction limiting candidate quality when all easy CSV-derivable axes have been exhausted'). The proposed Tiered Propose-Audit-Falsify-Commit method makes the escalation mechanical: step 5 now reads the Tier-A verdicts, and on Zero-SURVIVED branches into Tier-B which authorises exactly one raw-DBN feature (size imbalance, signed aggressor flow, quote intensity, time-since-trade, quote half-life) computed across every train date and falsified with the same pre-committed decision rule schema. The commit priority is changed so that 'weakest violation' is only legal when Tier-B was actually attempted — Tier-A-only weakest-violation picks are now a method violation that forces a method-failure paragraph and a prior-reasoning pick. Gate result: 0/5 metrics improved vs running-best loop 5 (pnl 780.50 vs 1471.75, sharpe 3.39 vs 13.72, max_dd -0.0386 vs -0.0164, win_rate 0.3543 vs 0.3547; mean_slippage tied). Action: reverted. If the new method works, the next reasoning trace will show: three Tier-A candidates with verdicts; on a Zero-SURVIVED branch, exactly one Tier-B raw-DBN feature with a literature anchor, a Tier-B regime audit across every train date, and a Tier-B falsification verdict with a pre-committed decision rule — the 'Where I felt uncertain' section will no longer list 'on-disk-CSV restriction' or 'weakest violation chosen despite no mechanism' as the dominant uncertainty.
